subject.title: Feature request: MEMORY.md size warning/limit enforcement

question: Should this issue be scoped to a warning-only Control UI budget indicator first, or should OpenClaw also block oversized MEMORY.md saves and/or auto-archive content?
rationale: Current main already has diagnostics, but save refusal and auto-archive change user memory editing and recovery semantics beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Ship warning-only first
options.body: Add an in-editor MEMORY.md budget indicator and non-blocking near-limit warning using the existing bootstrap budget analysis while leaving enforcement and archive behavior for separate decisions.

options.title: Block oversized saves
options.body: Make Control UI or `agents.files.set` refuse MEMORY.md saves over the configured bootstrap budget with a defined override and recovery path.

options.title: Design archive workflow separately
options.body: Treat auto-archive as a memory persistence feature with pointers, undo, and doctor or recovery integration before implementation.

recommendation.title: Ship warning-only first
recommendation.body: Add an in-editor MEMORY.md budget indicator and non-blocking near-limit warning using the existing bootstrap budget analysis while leaving enforcement and archive behavior for separate decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice spans gateway agent file RPCs, bootstrap behavior, and user-facing product semantics, where recent gateway/bootstrap history makes this the best available owner signal.
